goal: Introduce an explicit host-side translate scheduler at RHICommandList granularity, but move from a pure batch dispatch model to a streaming two-pipe model. VulkanSubmissionExecutor must expose Enqueue-style producer semantics, stream pending batches into a PreprocessPipe that emits immutable QueueTranslateInfo jobs plus GraphEventRef dependency edges, then enqueue those jobs into a TranslatePipe that records platform command buffers and optionally triggers GPU submit based on flush depth. Producer-side APIs remain single-producer for now, but fixed thread affinity is deferred. The scheduler contract must preserve enough executor-derived submit/sync information to support later policies that group multiple RHICommandList translate jobs into shared TranslateContext instances and reduce platform command-buffer count or submit count when profitable.

design_constraints.title: Command-list granularity only
design_constraints.detail: Phase 1 scheduling operates on whole RHICommandList / CmdSubmit translate jobs. No public sub-command-list API and no internal fine-grained translate slicing are allowed.

design_constraints.title: Executor stays immutable-orchestration only
design_constraints.detail: VulkanSubmissionExecutor may own batch canonicalization, preprocess snapshots, logical dependency extraction, translate-job assembly, and hand-off to submission runtime. It must not own execution-class scheduling policy, translate fence chaining policy, frontier publication, or mutable translate scheduling state.

design_constraints.title: Translate scheduling lives in VulkanTranslateTask
design_constraints.detail: Execution-class dispatch, explicit translate-fence waits, frontier consumption, translate completion publication, and any scheduler state machine must be implemented in VulkanTranslateTask or code owned by that unit.

design_constraints.title: GraphEventRef is the only host-side translate fence primitive
design_constraints.detail: RHITranslateFence must be a thin semantic wrapper over GraphEventRef. No second host-side synchronization model may be introduced for translate ordering.

design_constraints.title: Completion and boundary fences are distinct semantics
design_constraints.detail: The scheduler must distinguish one-job completion fences from aggregated boundary fences. Serial control completion may be required by later serial/frame-end work without automatically becoming the default wait target for later parallel work.

design_constraints.title: Serial is not a global barrier
design_constraints.detail: SerialControl jobs drain prior published frontiers before starting, but they do not automatically block future Parallel work unless explicitly published or explicitly waited by the caller.

design_constraints.title: FrameEnd is exclusive and drain-complete
design_constraints.detail: FrameEndExclusive must wait for all published frame-relevant frontiers and execute only after prior required translate work has completed.

design_constraints.title: GPU wait objects stay separate
design_constraints.detail: GraphEventRef-backed RHITranslateFence objects must never be reused as GPU WaitEvent or SignalEvent objects. Translate scheduling and GPU queue synchronization remain separate layers.

design_constraints.title: Structured testcase logs are mandatory
design_constraints.detail: TestRHITranslate must emit [TESTCASE][PASS|FAIL|SKIP] markers so PowerShell scripts can aggregate case-level results deterministically.

design_constraints.title: PowerShell scripts are the only validation entrypoints
design_constraints.detail: Validation continues only through testscripts/windows/test_rhi_translate.ps1 and testscripts/windows/test_all.ps1. No new primary wrapper becomes the main validation path.

design_constraints.title: Scheduler must preserve future TranslateContext policy freedom
design_constraints.detail: Phase 1 must not hard-code a permanent one-command-list to one-TranslateContext, one-platform-command-buffer, or one-submit mapping. Scheduler/job metadata must preserve enough executor-derived submit and sync information for later policies that merge multiple translate jobs into shared TranslateContext instances or fewer submits when ordering and lifetime constraints allow it.

design_constraints.title: Performance policy is data-driven, not baked into executor control flow
design_constraints.detail: Reducing platform command-buffer usage and reducing submit count are explicit performance goals, but the policy that trades them against parallel translate benefit must remain scheduler-owned and data-driven. Executor provides immutable submit/sync analysis; it must not accumulate ad-hoc mutable submit-merging logic.

execution_classes.name: Parallel
execution_classes.notes: Parallel work may additionally wait on explicit RHITranslateFence objects supplied by upper layers. It does not wait on the current serial frontier by default.

execution_classes.name: SerialControl
execution_classes.notes: Serial work drains prior published frontiers before it begins. It does not automatically publish itself as a default wait source for later parallel work.

execution_classes.name: FrameEndExclusive
execution_classes.notes: Frame-end runs only after all required translate work has drained and then resets frame-local frontier state.

frontiers.name: parallel_frontier
frontiers.meaning: Aggregated boundary for published parallel translate work.

frontiers.name: serial_frontier
frontiers.meaning: Latest published serial-control tail required by later serial/frame-end work.

frontiers.name: frame_frontier
frontiers.meaning: Aggregated boundary for all work that frame-end must drain.

future_policy_inputs.name: queue_affinity
future_policy_inputs.meaning: Which queue family or logical queue a translate job belongs to when considering shared TranslateContext reuse.

future_policy_inputs.name: submit_boundaries
future_policy_inputs.meaning: Executor-derived translated submit segmentation that a later policy may preserve or merge.

future_policy_inputs.name: sync_topology
future_policy_inputs.meaning: GPU wait/signal relationships and host-side explicit waits that constrain legal grouping.

future_policy_inputs.name: execution_class
future_policy_inputs.meaning: Parallel, SerialControl, and FrameEndExclusive semantics that constrain which jobs may share context or batch boundaries.

executor_responsibility_risk.detail: Executor already owns preprocess, segment planning, immutable dependency extraction, translate job assembly, and submit-info assembly. If translate scheduling policy is kept there, the file becomes the owner of both immutable analysis and mutable runtime scheduling state.

translate_task_gap.detail: TranslateTask currently only dispatches directly to queue.Translate and signals translate_complete. It does not yet own execution classes, translate fence waits, frontier consumption, or completion publication.

future_performance_policy_gap.detail: The current design discussion now requires future policies that let multiple RHICommandList translate jobs share one TranslateContext and reduce platform command-buffer usage or submit count. Phase 1 implementation must preserve the executor-derived submit/sync data needed for that policy without prematurely baking grouping heuristics into executor control flow.

test_gap.detail: Structured testcase markers and one additional multi-command-list ordering case are now in place, but scheduler-specific Parallel/SerialControl/FrameEnd cases are still missing.

structured_log_contract.owner: TestRHITranslate.exe emits these lines; PowerShell scripts parse and aggregate them.

future_scheduler_cases: parallel -> serial -> serial -> parallel -> serial ordering
serial completion not implicitly blocking later parallel work
parallel waiting on a selected serial fence only
frame-end exclusive draining all required frontiers
shared TranslateContext across multiple command-list translate jobs preserves correctness
scheduler policy reduces platform command-buffer count when submit merging is selected
scheduler policy reduces submit count when executor-derived submit/sync data permits submit merging
negative case: missing explicit wait triggers deterministic failure or assertion in test build

streaming_replan.why_replan_exists: The current implementation is a pure batch scheduler prototype. The next target is a streaming scheduler with explicit flush depth, user-visible translate-fence commands, and translate-stage lambda commands that remain ordered in the command stream.

confirmed_answers.flush_preprocess: RHITranslate only guarantees that the current pending batches have entered PreprocessPipe and that translate tasks plus their dependency edges have been enqueued toward TranslatePipe. It does not require translate completion and does not submit GPU work.
confirmed_answers.translate_fence_usage: RHITranslateFence is not merely a host wrapper returned by scheduler internals. The user inserts a TranslateFence command into RHICommandList, and the preprocess stage converts that command into scheduling metadata. Fence flags determine whether the current command list must first drain earlier translate work or whether the fence only blocks later translate tasks.
confirmed_answers.lambda_command_stage: LambdaCommand is a translate-stage host lambda. It executes in translate order, belongs to the user command stream, and must not be reordered away from adjacent user commands.
confirmed_answers.enqueue_naming: The executor API should be named Enqueue rather than Execute because it admits work into streaming task pipes instead of implying immediate execution semantics.
confirmed_answers.producer_thread_policy: Producer-side scheduler APIs remain single-producer for now. The exact thread-affinity contract is deferred and should not be hard-coded into Enqueue/Flush yet.

task_pipes.name: PreprocessPipe
task_pipes.role: Consumes pending VulkanSubmissionExecutor batches admitted by Enqueue() in streaming FIFO order, performs source-submit segmentation and dependency analysis, converts user TranslateFence commands into scheduler edges, and emits immutable QueueTranslateInfo jobs plus GraphEventRef dependencies.

task_pipes.name: TranslatePipe
task_pipes.role: Consumes preprocessed translate jobs, resolves host-side ordering from dependency events, runs translate recording, executes translate-stage lambda commands in-order, and optionally hands translated submits to submission runtime depending on flush depth.

flush_depths.name: RHITranslate
flush_depths.meaning: Push current pending batches into PreprocessPipe and finish dependency/job emission into TranslatePipe. No GPU submit is required and translate completion is not required.

flush_depths.name: SubmitGPU
flush_depths.meaning: Push current pending batches through preprocess, then ensure translated jobs are submitted to GPU submission runtime for all work included in this flush depth.

translate_fence_command_model.placement: The fence is authored by the user inside RHICommandList as an explicit command, not as an out-of-band scheduler-only handle.
translate_fence_command_model.preprocess_translation: PreprocessPipe converts fence commands into GraphEventRef-backed dependency/publication information on emitted QueueTranslateInfo jobs.
required_flag_semantics: a flag that makes the current command-list translate drain earlier translate work before it runs
a flag that publishes a fence so later translate tasks depend on this command list without forcing the current command list to drain earlier work

lambda_command_model.meaning: LambdaCommand remains embedded in the user command stream and executes in translate order as a host-side translate action. Reorder logic must treat it as a hard ordering boundary or opaque node rather than a command that may be redistributed freely.

constraints.title: Streaming replaces pure batch-only handoff
constraints.detail: The new mainline design is not a single DispatchBatch step. VulkanSubmissionExecutor::Enqueue must be able to stream pending batches into PreprocessPipe without immediately forcing a full translate-and-submit cycle.

constraints.title: Flush API must express depth explicitly
constraints.detail: A single Flush() with ambiguous semantics is insufficient. The API must distinguish at least RHITranslate and SubmitGPU so callers can choose whether work stops at preprocess/translate dispatch or continues to GPU submission.

constraints.title: TranslateFence is a user command, not an internal wrapper only
constraints.detail: Users author translate fence intent inside RHICommandList. The scheduler may still lower that intent to GraphEventRef-based dependencies internally, but the public usage model is command-based.

constraints.title: Translate-stage lambda is ordering-sensitive
constraints.detail: LambdaCommand executes during translate and must not be reordered away from neighboring user commands. Reorder must treat it as opaque and preserve visible user ordering.

constraints.title: Executor owns streaming preprocess only
constraints.detail: Executor may own batch intake, preprocess scheduling, segmentation, and dependency graph construction. It must not become the owner of mutable translate runtime state, TranslateContext reuse policy, or GPU submit-merging heuristics.

constraints.title: Producer APIs stay single-producer without fixed affinity
constraints.detail: Enqueue and flush-depth APIs must still be used from one producer thread at a time, but the implementation must not hard-code render-thread-only validation until the wider runtime contract is finalized.

checkpoints.title: Freeze scheduler semantics and job metadata at command-list granularity
checkpoints.problem: The project needs a stable phase-1 scheduler contract before any implementation starts, otherwise execution order and responsibility boundaries will keep drifting between executor and translate task.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: Parallel, SerialControl, and FrameEndExclusive are the only phase-1 execution classes.
Scheduling granularity is whole RHICommandList / CmdSubmit translate job.
Upper layers explicitly choose execution class and any explicit translate waits.
tasks: Define execution-class metadata carried with each translate job.
Define explicit wait-fence input carried with each translate job.
Define publication targets or publish-mask semantics for translate completion.
Preserve executor-derived submit/sync metadata needed by future TranslateContext-sharing and submit-merging policy.

checkpoints.title: Move translate scheduling policy out of VulkanSubmissionExecutor
checkpoints.problem: Executor currently assembles translate jobs and is the natural place where scheduling policy could accidentally accumulate, which would make the file own both immutable preprocessing and mutable execution behavior.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: Executor only assembles immutable translate-job descriptors and hands them off.
VulkanTranslateTask owns translate scheduling behavior and host-side wait resolution.
No new execution-policy state machine is added to VulkanSubmissionExecutor.cpp.
tasks: Keep preprocess and logical dependency extraction in VulkanSubmissionExecutor.cpp.
Move translate wait resolution, frontier consumption, and completion publication into VulkanTranslateTask-owned code.
Reject any implementation that adds long-lived scheduler mutable state into executor.
Keep future TranslateContext grouping and submit-merging policy scheduler-owned rather than executor-owned.

checkpoints.title: Implement RHITranslateFence and frontier chaining
checkpoints.problem: Selective chained waits such as 'serial2 drains prior work but does not block parallel2 by default' require a first-class distinction between completion fences and aggregated boundary frontiers.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: RHITranslateFence is a thin GraphEventRef-backed host-side translate fence.
Completion and boundary fence semantics are distinct.
parallel_frontier, serial_frontier, and frame_frontier are updated by explicit publication rules.
tasks: Define RHITranslateFence kind metadata.
Implement boundary aggregation on top of GraphEventRef chaining.
Implement default wait rules for Parallel, SerialControl, and FrameEndExclusive.
Ensure GraphEventRef-based fences never cross into GPU WaitEvent/SignalEvent code paths.

checkpoints.title: Integrate frame-end exclusive draining
checkpoints.problem: Frame-end RHI tail work needs stronger semantics than ordinary serial control; it must run only after all required translate work for the frame has drained and must reset frame-local frontier state cleanly.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: FrameEndExclusive waits for all required published frontiers before executing.
Frame-end translate logic is modeled as scheduler behavior rather than ad-hoc executor-only sequencing.
Frame-local frontiers are reset in one explicit place after frame-end completion.
tasks: Define how frame-end jobs consume frame_frontier and serial/parallel tails.
Define when frontier reset occurs and who owns it.
Keep frame-end execution semantics out of executor-specific ad-hoc logic.

checkpoints.title: Expand scheduler test suite and lock the script contract
checkpoints.problem: Without scheduler-specific tests and a stable case-level aggregation contract, future scheduler work can silently regress selective waits, serial publication rules, or frame-end draining behavior.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: Scheduler-specific cases are present in TestRHITranslate.
PowerShell scripts fail when structured testcase markers are missing or when any structured case fails.
The validation baseline covers both existing translate behavior and new scheduler semantics.
tasks: Add explicit Parallel/SerialControl/FrameEnd scheduler cases to TestRHITranslate.
Keep test_rhi_translate.ps1 and test_all.ps1 parsing the standardized testcase markers.
Reject new scheduler behavior that cannot be expressed as deterministic case-level results in the existing scripts.

checkpoints.title: Add TranslateContext sharing and submit-merging policy on top of scheduler metadata
checkpoints.problem: The scheduler must eventually optimize platform command-buffer usage and submit count, but that policy should be implemented only after explicit execution classes, waits, and frontier semantics are stable.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: Multiple translate jobs may share one TranslateContext when policy selects merging.
Platform command-buffer count can be reduced without violating execution order or resource lifetime constraints.
Submit count can be reduced when executor-derived submit/sync topology proves submit merging is legal.
Policy decisions remain data-driven and do not leak ad-hoc mutable logic back into VulkanSubmissionExecutor.cpp.
tasks: Define the scheduler-owned policy input view over queue affinity, submit boundaries, sync topology, and execution class.
Implement TranslateContext sharing rules that preserve serial and frame-end semantics.
Implement optional submit-merging rules and measure when they should be preferred over extra parallelism.
Add deterministic tests for shared TranslateContext correctness and reduced submit behavior.

checkpoints.title: Replace pure batch translate dispatch with streaming PreprocessPipe and TranslatePipe
checkpoints.problem: The current design prototype translates an already assembled batch in one step. That is insufficient for streaming flush depth and for future scheduler policies that need preprocess and translate to advance independently.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: VulkanSubmissionExecutor::Enqueue streams pending batches into a dedicated PreprocessPipe.
PreprocessPipe emits immutable QueueTranslateInfo jobs and GraphEventRef dependencies rather than directly performing translate dispatch.
TranslatePipe consumes preprocessed jobs independently of executor batch intake.
tasks: Introduce explicit PreprocessPipe ownership in VulkanSubmissionExecutor state.
Introduce explicit TranslatePipe ownership for translate job dispatch.
Rename Execute semantics to Enqueue semantics at the public API boundary.
Define the handoff contract from preprocess output to translate-pipe enqueue.

checkpoints.title: Add explicit flush depth for preprocess-only versus submit-gpu progression
checkpoints.problem: A single Flush() entrypoint cannot express whether the caller wants only preprocess/translate dispatch setup or wants GPU submit issuance as well.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: RHITranslate guarantees pending batches are admitted to PreprocessPipe and translate jobs/dependencies are emitted toward TranslatePipe.
SubmitGPU guarantees pending work advances through preprocess and reaches GPU submit issuance.
API names and completion semantics are explicit rather than inferred from call context.
tasks: Define a public flush-depth enum or equivalent API shape.
Use RHITranslate and SubmitGPU as the flush-depth names.
Thread flush-depth semantics through VulkanSubmissionExecutor and the executor-facing RHI API.
Define which events, if any, each flush depth returns for optional synchronization.

checkpoints.title: Defer fixed producer-thread affinity for Enqueue and flush-depth APIs
checkpoints.problem: The current producer-thread contract is not finalized. Enqueue and flush-depth progression should not be hard-wired to render-thread-only validation until the wider runtime ownership model is settled.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: Producer APIs remain single-producer.
Render-thread-only validation is not baked into the executor prematurely.
Any future affinity rule is introduced only after the runtime contract is explicitly confirmed.
tasks: Keep the public producer API shape compatible with a future affinity rule without enforcing one yet.
Document that current code should not bootstrap or validate render-thread identity for Enqueue/Flush.
Revisit the exact affinity model only after the runtime threading contract is explicitly confirmed.

checkpoints.title: Redesign RHITranslateFence as a user-authored command-stream primitive
checkpoints.problem: The current internal wrapper model does not match intended usage. Users need to author translate-fence intent inside RHICommandList so preprocess can derive dependency edges directly from command order.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: RHICommandList exposes a TranslateFence command primitive authored by the user.
Preprocess converts TranslateFence commands into dependency/publication metadata for QueueTranslateInfo jobs.
Fence flags distinguish at least 'drain-before-current' and 'publish-for-later' semantics.
tasks: Define the public command shape and flag set for TranslateFence.
Add preprocess logic that turns fence commands into GraphEventRef dependency edges.
Keep GPU wait/signal synchronization separate from translate-fence semantics.

checkpoints.title: Add translate-stage LambdaCommand and make reorder preserve it as opaque ordering
checkpoints.problem: Users need translate-stage host callbacks embedded in the command stream, but existing reorder logic treats generic custom commands as reorderable command content and does not encode the stronger ordering guarantee required here.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: LambdaCommand can be authored inside RHICommandList.
LambdaCommand executes during translate as a host-side action.
Command reorder preserves LambdaCommand placement relative to adjacent user commands.
tasks: Define LambdaCommand command type and execution callback contract.
Teach preprocess and translate paths how to carry LambdaCommand without lowering it into reorderable shader-resource analysis only.
Mark LambdaCommand as an opaque ordering boundary in RHICmdReorderer and translate recording.

checkpoints.title: Carry TranslateContext sharing and submit merging into the streaming scheduler model
checkpoints.problem: Once preprocess and translate are streamed independently, TranslateContext sharing and submit merging must be expressed against streamed job metadata and flush depth rather than against a monolithic batch only.
what_must_be_true_after_this_checkpoint: TranslateContext reuse decisions operate on streamed QueueTranslateInfo jobs and their dependency graph.
Submit-merging decisions respect flush depth and TranslateFence/LambdaCommand ordering semantics.
Scheduler-owned policy remains data-driven and does not leak back into executor control flow.
tasks: Extend policy inputs to include flush depth and pipe-stage boundaries.
Define legal merge windows in the presence of user-authored TranslateFence commands and LambdaCommand ordering boundaries.
Add deterministic tests for context sharing and submit reduction under the streaming model.

analysis_notes.why_new_json_exists: Translate scheduler work should not be mixed into descriptor-heap checkpoints. It has a separate ownership split, separate synchronization model, and separate testing contract.
analysis_notes.main_design_risk: If VulkanSubmissionExecutor keeps accumulating mutable scheduling policy, the scheduler will become another monolithic runtime center and upper-layer execution-class decisions will stop being explicit.
analysis_notes.main_testing_risk: If structured testcase markers stop being required, PowerShell scripts will fall back to coarse executable pass/fail and scheduler-specific regressions will be much harder to isolate.
analysis_notes.future_policy_note: TranslateContext sharing and submit merging are treated as scheduler-owned policies built on top of stable execution-class, fence, pipe-stage, and flush-depth semantics rather than as assumptions hard-coded into phase-1 control flow.
analysis_notes.streaming_replan_note: The pure batch DispatchBatch prototype is no longer the target architecture. It is now treated as a transitional prototype that must be replaced by a streaming PreprocessPipe plus TranslatePipe model with explicit flush depth.
analysis_notes.user_confirmed_semantics: User confirmed that TranslateFence is authored as a command-stream primitive, LambdaCommand runs during translate and must remain opaque to reorder, Execute should be renamed to Enqueue, fixed producer-thread affinity should be deferred for now, and the flush-depth names should be RHITranslate and SubmitGPU.
analysis_notes.implemented_execute_order: Implemented order is Enqueue -> PreprocessPipe -> TranslatePipe -> SubmissionRuntime. Flush(RHITranslate) stops after translate-task emission, while Flush(SubmitGPU) additionally drains submission-runtime intake.
